summary: POC scoping call to agree success criteria, workload sizing, timeline, and open-model candidates for Omnitect. Customer cares about multilingual performance (EN/ES/PT/FR), domain-specific legal/finance accuracy, and strict data residency/VPC controls. Agreed next steps: share model shortlist and perf matrix, customer to send sample data, schedule benchmark run mid-March.
transcript:
[00:00] Raj (AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. quick roll call?
[00:06] Priya (CTO): Priya here, Dan and Marcus and Sofia are on my side.
[00:10] Raj: Great, we got Lena our solutions engineer and Amir from CSM. agenda is POC scoping for open-models, focus on success criteria, sizing, benchmarks, timeline. sound good?
[00:18] Dan (ML Eng): Yep sounds good. quick note, we're evaluating non-proprietary models due to licensing.
[00:23] Lena (SE): Nice. quick question before we dive: are there hard latency SLOs or more cost-driven?
[00:30] Marcus (Head of AI): Both. ideally tail latency under 300ms 99p for short-form Q&A, but for longer generations we can accept up to 1s. cost is also a big driver, we can't multiply token costs by 10x.
[00:42] Priya: Also must support Spanish and Portuguese well, and be conservative on hallucinations for legal/contract summaries. data residency — we need VPC and KMS options.
[00:52] Raj: Perfect, that's helpful. I'm just taking note: success criteria = accuracy on legal/finance prompts, multilingual recall, latency under 300ms for short queries, cost threshold X (we'll quantify).
[01:05] Lena: For bench plan we'll need a representative prompt set and sample documents. Dan, can you share the sample dataset?
[01:11] Dan: Yes will do, we have 1k anonymized contract snippets and 500 Q&A pairs across en/es/pt.
[01:18] Raj: Excellent. now on model shortlist: we typically recommend testing 3-4 open models to balance perf/cost/quality. preliminary candidates: Llama 2-Chat 70B (quantized), Mistral Large / Mixtral variants, Falcon-40B-instruct, and BLOOMZ for multilingual. also note Mistral x with finetune if needed.
[01:36] Marcus: quick clarifying q — how does Redwood handle quantized vs fp16 variants? like impact on hallucination and latency?
[01:43] Lena: short answer: quantization gives big latency/cost wins but sometimes small accuracy regressions, especially on specialized legal phrasing. we can run both quantized (4-bit) and fp16 baselines in the same POC. Redwood runtime supports kernel selection per-variant so we can compare.
[01:58] Priya: Are there pre-built legal domain adapters available?
[02:01] Lena: not off-the-shelf for every model; we can test few-shot prompts and lightweight adapter or instruction-finetune. for the POC we'll focus on zero/few-shot plus prompt engineering before proposing finetune.
[02:14] Raj: Let's talk workload sizing — Dan, what's expected qps and token distribution?
[02:18] Dan: steady-state 15 qps, peak 80 qps for bursts; average prompt length 120 tokens, average completion 240 tokens. monthly tokens roughly 150M.
[02:30] Amir (CSM): good to flag that Dedicated capacity could help for predictable throughput; hosted with autoscaling is cheaper initially.
[02:38] Priya: We prefer hosted for speed of evaluation but will need VPC/private later for regs.
[02:44] Raj: timeline — propose benchmark setup week of 3/16, run 3-5 models in parallel, compare quality (ROUGE/BLEU + human label on hallucinations), latency p95/p99, and cost per 1k tokens. follow-up review 3/19. ok?
[02:58] Marcus: that works. can you quantify cost-per-1k token for each model rough order?
[03:03] Raj: roughs: quantized Llama-70B ~ $0.20/1k tokens, Mistral Large quantized ~ $0.12, Falcon-40B ~ $0.09, BLOOMZ maybe $0.14. those are ballpark and vary by compile/kernels and batching.
[03:18] Dan: those numbers help — our budget target is under $0.15/1k on average.
[03:22] Lena: a note on batching: for your latency SLOs we might limit batch windows to 20-30ms. that reduces efficiency but hits latency. Redwood Optimize can later suggest batching profiles to meet cost goals.
[03:35] Priya: about multilingual capability — BLOOMZ is strong but older; Mistral community models have decent EN/ES but PT is meh in many models. how do we measure?
[03:44] Lena: we'll add language buckets to the benchmark and a small human eval panel for ES/PT. also use cross-lingual QA hits and hallucination rates.
[03:52] Raj: security checklist: SOC2 available, we support KMS/HSM integrations and VPC private endpoints. Amir will send the onboarding checklist and security artifacts.
[03:59] Amir: noted, will share SOC2 report, ISO attestation, and VPC playbook.
[04:05] Sofia (Product): one open question — do you support function/tool calling or structured outputs for extraction tasks?
[04:10] Lena: yes we support structured outputs and function-like calls; for extraction we can run constrained decoders and validate with schema checks. we'll include examples in the bench harness.
[04:19] Priya: timeline for onboarding to run benchmarks — how long to get a hosted benchmark running after we share data?
[04:24] Raj: typically 2-3 business days to ingest samples and configure harness; bench runs a day or two per model depending on sizing. so week of 3/16 is feasible.
[04:33] Marcus: curious about fallback policies — if a quantized model misses a quality threshold, can Redwood route requests to a stronger model automatically?
[04:40] Lena: yes, smart routing supports policy-based fallback by latency/cost/quality. you can set thresholds to route to a higher-quality variant for problematic prompts.
[04:49] Dan: how do you measure per-prompt quality in real-time to trigger fallback?
[04:53] Lena: we can use a lightweight classifier or scoring hook; for POC we'll run offline detection and then discuss a real-time scoring approach for production.
[05:01] Raj: ok let's surface success criteria again: 1) human-rated accuracy >= 90% on contract summary tasks, 2) hallucination rate under 5% on legal prompts, 3) average latency under 300ms for short Qs, 4) cost < $0.15/1k tokens. Any objections?
[05:15] Priya: sounds reasonable, might move accuracy threshold to 92% depending on results but start at 90.
[05:20] Marcus: agree. one more — we need the bench to include edge-case legal templates we have.
[05:25] Raj: Dan will include those.
[05:28] Sophia (sic) -- (transcription noise) Speaker 1: sorry small cross talk.
[05:35] Lena: for evaluation metrics we'll track ROUGE for summarization, exact match for extraction, human hallucination tags, latency p95/p99, and cost per 1k tokens.
[05:44] Priya: on compliance — we will want logs for auditing, but redwood retaining payloads is a no-go; do you support no-retain mode?
[05:50] Amir: yes, we support customer-controlled retention and customer-managed KMS; logs can be sent to customer's SIEM via secure delivery.
[05:57] Dan: curious about fine-tuning timeline if we need it — what's typical?
[06:01] Lena: small instruction finetune or LoRA can be done in a couple weeks; we would first evaluate prompt-engineering and adapter approaches during the POC and only propose finetune if necessary.
[06:11] Raj: okay last part: deliverables from Redwood for the POC — shortlist + perf cost matrix, benchmark plan, containerized harness + runbook, and security docs. we'll also provide a scheduling link for the 3/19 review.
[06:23] Priya: good. who owns the bench run?
[06:26] Lena: Redwood SE will run it but we need Dan to provide samples and labeling guidance.
[06:31] Raj: thanks everyone. quick recap and confirm next steps: I'll send shortlist + rough cost numbers by Monday 3/9; Amir sends SOC2 and VPC checklist by 3/8; Dan sends sample data by 3/10; bench runs week of 3/16; follow-up review 3/19.
[06:47] Priya: that timeline looks good to us.
[06:50] Marcus: any blockers on our side, we'll flag.
[06:54] Raj: perfect, we'll record action items in CRM and share calendar invites. thanks all.
[06:59] [END] 

Notes on transcript quality: occasional speaker mislabels and small transcription errors ("Sophia" instead of "Sofia"). Some timestamps are approximate. Bench artifacts mentioned: https://redwood.app/decks/omnitect-poc and sample bench harness repo link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-harness (demo placeholder).
